content:
The game itself is fine. The main chat, however, is a completely different story.

author: Mawors
title: Great experiences, needs some little improvements.
content:
I’ve read the comments, and I’m actively playing the game. I think the classes were well designed, but with every season the differences between them become more noticeable, especially in terms of disadvantages. The rankings already show the reality of the game: the top players are mostly P2W, which is understandable…if you spend money, that’s part of the benefit. However, the developers should test PvP between classes using similar levels and stats. The gap in performance between some classes is huge, and this also affects PvE progression.

Exploration also has too many restrictions: level requirements, rank, damage requirements, keys, special tools, etc. It’s frustrating to know that in 24 hours I’ll finally unlock the next area, only to realize that I’m already much stronger than the recommended level and then have to wait another 24 hours for the next one. Progression should be based more on level ranges and offer several areas at the same time. Otherwise, the game becomes repetitive.

I also thought buying some items would improve my experience, but honestly, it didn’t make much difference.

I understand that it’s impossible to satisfy everyone, but there are definitely things that could be improved. Events are another example. Some have unique rewards, but the dance event felt like spending time just to collect a few notes. The recent minigames have been more entertaining, though.

The whale event was especially confusing because there was no real introduction or explanation of the collaboration. Not everyone playing the game knows anime or shows from other countries. Even a short introduction explaining what the whale is and why we are fighting it would help a lot. Right now, I’m sure many players are just hunting it for the special coins without even knowing what the whale represents.

Overall, I like the game, but I think improving class balance, exploration progression, and event explanations would make the experience much better.

author: Daddy3667746
title: So Much Potential, Unfortunately Buried Under P2W
content:
This game has so much potential. It genuinely feels like playing an MMO on your phone, and there are a lot of things here that I really enjoy. Unfortunately, the longer I play, the more obvious it becomes where this game seems to be headed.

The Good

Character customization
The character customization is actually really cool and surprisingly unique. There are a lot of ways to make your character feel like your own.

Skills and class variety
Each class has numerous skills, and the order in which you use them actually matters. There is some real depth to combat, and I like that different classes can fill traditional MMO roles.

Collectible outfits
The different outfits are a fun addition and give you another way to customize your character.

Characters, story, and voice acting
I was honestly surprised by this. The characters and story aren’t bad at all, and the voice acting is actually pretty good. It makes the world feel more like a real MMO rather than just another mobile game.

Tank / Healer / DPS roles
You can actually build traditional MMO parties with tanks, healers, and DPS. That’s something I really appreciate because it gives the game more of that classic MMO feeling.

Dungeons and boss fights
Being able to run dungeons and fight bosses with actual players is great. These are some of the moments where the game really feels like a legitimate MMO on your phone.

Pets
They’re cute. That’s pretty much it. 

Arena
The Arena is decent and adds another thing to do.

Auction House
The fact that there is an actual Auction House is a HUGE positive. This could have been one of the features that really sets this game apart from other mobile MMOs.

Unfortunately, there’s a pretty major problem with it, which brings me to the bad.

The Bad

You guessed it: It’s P2W. Heavily.

There are numerous progression paths that are blocked by vines, stone pillars, and other obstacles. Yes, you can remove them using items that are technically obtainable for free, but those items cost an absolute fortune.

And there are WAY too many of these obstacles.

I’m currently looking at 12 different paths on my map that I can’t access because I don’t have the required items. It’s incredibly frustrating to look at all of these areas and know that I can’t reasonably access them without spending a ridiculous amount of resources.

Exploration should make you excited to see what’s around the next corner. Instead, I’m constantly running into another obstacle and thinking, “Well, I guess I’m not going there.”

The Auction House

This could have been a feature that genuinely sets this game apart.

But, of course, the only currency you can use in the Auction House is premium currency.

So essentially, you’re buying and trading items using real-money currency. And that creates a situation where whales can dominate the entire market and continue pulling further and further ahead.

If you’re F2P—or even close to it—the Auction House might as well not exist for you.

It’s essentially a marketplace for whales to trade with other whales.

SO. MANY. THINGS. TO. BUY.

The game constantly pushes purchases at you.

There is FOMO everywhere, and it feels extremely predatory.

Like most games in this genre, you’re eventually going to hit walls. Maybe you need more power. Maybe you need a certain item. Maybe you’re blocked from progressing somewhere.

And then, conveniently…

“For only $5.99, you can get just enough power to move forward!”

Big surprise.

The problem isn’t that the game has things you can buy. I’m completely fine with games making money. The problem is that the game seems to constantly create obstacles and then present spending money as the solution.

Conclusion

This is the frustrating part:

I genuinely think this game could be incredible.

There is something special here. The MMO mechanics, classes, customization, dungeons, parties, skills, story, and overall presentation have a ton of potential.

If this game were subscription-based, I honestly think I’d have a hard time putting it down.

I know this will probably fall on deaf ears, but the F2P community really needs a win.

Give us a subscription option. Create separate servers for whales and F2P players. Reduce the paywalls. Make the Auction House usable without premium currency. Give players a reasonable way to explore and progress without constantly feeling like they’re being pushed toward the cash shop.

Do something.

Because the foundation of this game is genuinely good.

author: Zantis12
title: A good game with room for improvement
content:
I wrote a review before but after playing to the end of the fourth area and trying all the classes I decided to write an updated one. While I like the game and it’s fun the class balance issues are a big problem. There are four classes and their name changes after each upgrade. There is a tank class, a melee dps, a magic dps and a healer class. 

Unfortunately the magic dps class is so much better than the others that it’s by far the most played. The dps magic class gets every element except darkness , the most damage dealing potential the most class synergy and versatility. The others classes just can’t compete with it. 

The healer class gets healing and support spells and darkness element for decent damage. They also get some summon pet abilities but the pets die so fast and  don’t do much damage so they are useless. The healer class is decent but very boring to play and you don’t see many.

The tank class has  water and light elements and some tanking and physical skills. They don’t really become good at tanking until they get the passive ability to reduce damage from taunted enemies late into the game. The tank class is probably the worst in the game. While it can draw aggro the class isn’t very durable for what it’s supposed to do and their armor gets punched through by bosses like it’s made of paper. It also has the lowest dps in the game making it subpar in every way. 

The melee dps has fire and darkness elements and physical skills and is somewhere in between the tank and magic dps class. They don’t have taunt but are very hard to kill with skills like indomitable will which is just a much better version of the self revive skill the actual tank has. They also have some passive abilities that make them stronger as they lose health both offensively and defensively making the tank class almost obsolete. The only downside is they don’t have a lot of synergy with their passive abilities so it can be hard to build a good skill set with them.

The other aspect of character strategy is the fantomon. Once you grow them into an adult it is like having a second character. While they are my favorite part of the game they could use some rebalancing. You hardly ever see any used except the two mystic rarity ones. The others could definitely use some buffs to make them more competitive and useful in combat. 

The only other gripe I have with the game is how little effort is put into your own character’s appearance. You can customize the costume and look of them but the portrait of them is always the default white hair and red eyes with a different color background based on your class. You don’t even get to use any of the outfits you get from dungeons because the developers want to sell you costumes for real money. It’s a shame considering the developers try to use attractive female characters to sale the game in the ads you see for it. The npcs look well drawn so I don’t see why the one you will play as for 100s of hours potential can’t have the portrait be more personalized.

author: aken4
title: Simple but if you wanna compete need to spend a lot of money
content:
You get exp points from just waiting is nice, a lot of helping out each other and straight forward mechanics for dungeons and battles.  Don’t have to think too much of HP, def, speed, atk, etc numbers since they total it as power.  That’s how you unlock areas, you can be under leveled but some classes and set ups allows some wiggle room.  Easy to switch class if you get bored of one and equipments, pets, skills are leveled up as slots so don’t need to hoard materials for specific equipment.  So if you casually wanna play it’s fun.  

Problems:
Servers are not fully merged so if you don’t start the same time as your friends, you are lucked out, even in  the future it might never merge if you start so far apart.  You are significantly at disadvantage the later you start in the server.  Because you only earn XP as you let the time roll.  The numbers of players are quite limited in servers so once server gets full you can’t get anymore new guild members which really sucks, because guild battles you’re at disadvantage because you can’t get anymore new recruits.

Also if you want to be competitive you have to start early once new server start and spend ton of money to speed up your leveling. So there is auction you can do in game for equipment you pick up in game that you don’t use.  which game charges you fee to list it (premium stones).  And the people who dived in to dungeon early and got lucky with equipment sells in auction.  And these auction can go easy as $50 per equipment, and new area weapons right now are $300 US per weapon/equipment.  And these dungeons you can only dive 2 times a day for free to play and collect random drops and guaranteed equipment shards (100 needed to complete 1 equipment). You can spend premium stones for 2 more times.  
There are companion characters that you unlock but not much voice interactions in game like other phone games which is disappointing.  There’s little interaction via text but that’s it.  No marrying option.  I think it’s just US version but voice acting is bit of cringe.  I honestly could not get into story like other games on phone.

Descent game to pass time nothing more

This game has such great bones and is pretty good from an afk standpoint. That’s pretty much where the good ends. Every single thing in this game is geared to make players spend or want to spend. I’ve been playing since day one and have done well to keep up, but have watched my server go from 100’s of active players all the way down to 100 at best. Many of those on the top 100 have actually quit and are still strong enough to be there. 

My honest opinion is that this game, and probably mobile gaming in general, have pushed so hard into microtransactions and almost forcing people into them to enjoy the game even a little that it’s just too far gone to say it’s entertainment.

It very clearly favors high spenders but doles out the micro transactions in small portions over time.  They place higher cost transactions at crucial points of progression to give spenders a larger advantage over free to play players.

author: Rav3nClawX
title: Best Mobile RPG ever
content:
I’ve played mobile MMOs for over a decade, and Sword x Staff is the first one in a long time that kept me logging in because I wanted to, not because I felt forced to.

The class system is incredible. Being able to mix skills and experiment with different builds means there isn’t just one “correct” way to play. I’ve spent hours testing damage, refining my setup, and every improvement feels earned. Boss fights are challenging, progression is satisfying, and watching your character grow from weak to unbelievably powerful never gets old.

The world is beautiful, the soundtrack is great, and the idle mechanics respect your time without taking away from active gameplay. Whether you want to grind, theorycraft, or just explore, there’s something here for you.

No game is perfect, but the developers have built an RPG with real depth and tons of potential. If they continue adding classes, skills, raids, and endgame content, this could become one of the best mobile MMORPGs on the market.

10/10. I came for the isekai theme… I stayed because the gameplay is genuinely addictive.

author: Lorethea
title: Awesome game!
content:
I have been enjoying this game for a month or so. It’s amazing.

The art is adorable. There are so many things to do each day to level. The guild and grouping set up is so great. I actually interact with people because the game is designed to be played with others.

It feels like a MMO on my phone, which is awesome.

The dungeons are basically automatic, so it’s been nice to go into a dungeon while I’m doing work on the computer or whatever else I’m doing. And if you do have to alt-tab out of the game, you still get all your loot. Hopefully you don’t let your team down by not healing yourself or something, but it’s really not annoying if people do.

You get 4 dungeon rewards a day, but it’s dependent on people queueing, and since I’m studying on a laptop, I just constantly queue.

There are no ads. So great. But that means we need to pay them for their work other ways. Therefore, this is the first app I actually make purchases from. My first purchase was great - I bought it and instantly got it. 

Last week Apple notified me of a charge by them I didn’t purchase. I didn’t notice items in my account, as I may have left the $15 charge if I did get stuff. There was no way to know what it was for or ask about it, so I refused the charge… and was auto banned. ☹️

I took screenshots of my account and the charge. It took a day, but they lifted it as soon as they got the information.

I bet people are trying to steal from them, and they’re already not getting money from ads. That’s terrible.

You definitely do not have make any purchases to stay in the top 5% of players if you’re farming your daily stuff, but this game is absolutely worth giving some extra money to for all their hard work and their lovely mmo they have developed for us. Also, their customer service is great.

author: NekoTheSpook
title: Finally, a perfect AFK
content: I’ve been playing this game for about a month, and I am completely hooked. First off, the system is set so you will level up whether you’re actively logged in or not. Most games of this type in my experience that label themselves ‘AFK’ may collect resources while you are logged out, and I can’t think of any that actually give you experience points without paying for a pass or auto-gatherer. Not so with S&S - it’s a pleasure to open your game and discover your character has leveled up while you were away. Another really nice feature is you can change your class, and keep your levels. No more multiple accounts just to try them all! I have also enjoyed the crossover events; the mini games are great, and you can collect outfits, hairstyles, and weapons without spending a ridiculous amount. In fact, I’m amazed that this is a free-to-play game with NO ADS. The rewards are very generous, and you can get surprisingly far without spending anything. (Do spend a little, they truly deserve it). But I think the biggest pull for me is the graphics & design quality. Spend a little time on the Home screen, just to watch shooting stars and fireflies. Look for the shadows of whales swimming overhead in Aqualis battles. The entire game is polished and it’s obvious that care went into the world crafting. Gameplay is easy to pick up, and addictive enough to keep you coming back for more. So, my message to the devs: you have created a game that’s just what I was looking for, except I didn’t know it until I played it. Thank you for making such a fantastic, beautiful world to explore!

author: JigokuMan
title: Pay to Win / Odd Timegating
content:
There's a functional dopamine loop here, and that's about the nicest thing I can say. 

While I don’t mind paying for skins or additional content, everything else feels engineered to separate you from your wallet, not to make a good game. 

Pay-to-win isn't a feature, it's the foundation. Limited-time offers, premium advancement tracks, it's relentless. This isn't monetization bolted onto a game; the game was built around the monetization. And don’t forget the ranking system, it’s like look at this person, they spent and absolute ****ton of cash. 

The story is an afterthought. "Chaos exists, get ‘er <adventurer>" is genuinely the entire narrative. Clearing a zone gives you nothing, no weight, no payoff. And they couldn't even leave exploration alone… 100% completion is locked behind unique keys, which are locked behind purchases, which may even be locked until you get to the next zone. 

Companions are a rough draft. The visage leveling system had potential, but the dialogue reads like it skipped both translation and editing. It’s distracting in a bad way. 

Will I continue? Probably not. The flashy combos were interesting at first, but the shine is wearing off and there really isn’t anything to keep you there.

author: Based&Ice-Pilled
title: God awful, mind numbing game
content:
I preordered this game when I saw it on the App Store. I didn't quite expect a masterpiece, so my standards for this game were low. Somehow, this game even failed to reach that mark. This game is the definition of pointless. Everything is a numbers game. It’s one of those awful types of games where all you do is continuously upgrade your stuff so that you can watch a big number grow even bigger. Mind numbing slop at its finest.

One of the things that made me quit this game in under a week were the ridiculous ads they started putting out after the game launched. It’s blatant false advertising much like how other slop games advertise themselves. Some defenders may try to say “but the developers don’t control or make the ads.” Sure, but there’s a thing called quality control. Clearly the developers are content that these misleading ads are getting people to download the game. They know they COULD do better, they just choose not to, and instead fake their work. Pathetic.

For actual gameplay, there’s essentially almost none. It’s all an illusion of progress. You wander around a meaningless world with meaningless characters in it. You’ll find yourself quickly being gated by enemies with power levels much higher than your own, forcing you to upgrade your gear. You’ll probably spend more time in menus managing your trash than actually doing anything. After upgrading things, you’ll inevitably run out of materials, forcing you to AFK for resources. THAT’S NOT GAMEPLAY. I honestly don’t know which is worse for the illusion of gameplay: grinding or AFK nonsense. I don’t even know why this game calls itself a “third way RPG” (what does that even mean lol???), it’s just gachaslop that’ll EOS in less than 5 years. 

The gacha in this game isn’t too bad, I guess (though I’ve heard in that in a recent collab event they were already getting P2W with that). You gamble for skills, pets, or relics. Boring stuff like that. This game feels very lifeless. I wouldn’t even be surprised if some of the players on the leaderboard are just bots created by the developers. I can’t imagine anyone actually spending thousands of dollars on this trash game. The story and characters are similarly lifeless. They are bland and exist solely to drive you through one land so you can move onto the next. Character designs are painfully generic too. The voice acting is obnoxious or highly questionable at best.

If you’d like to keep your brain cells, don’t even give this game a chance.

author: SxS Mr.Wilson
title: Honest Review
content:
Check it out people, the game is not bad in its core but lacks in a few areas. As someone who is busy its not bad as you can progress the gabe but get stuck every day so 30 min is enough for you to catch up. On the other side someone with more time is not able to do anything as you’re stuck getting all of your exp from idling. 

This feature sucks.

Dont expect to have fun following the campaign in the game because you will only be able to experience it once every other day making the story (which is well written) fall apart as you try to remember what happened last. 

Getting level locked and out powered by people who spend way too much money on the game is a hard pill to swallow when you are trying to be an active and helpful player.

I get that the devs need support and I even got the passes and other things since I like to show my support but they really need to change the exp system or at least not level block the players as much.

The resources are gettable but not abundant and make your progress feel slow as you may bet one or two weapons and skills upgraded a day. 

Gifts for your companions are slow and you dont get enough to feel like your making good progress after 4-5 companions are collected.

The event felt slow and pay to win to even participate even though it took a bit of effort to clear.

All in all its a good game and fun to play but has a-lot of drawbacks.    

I will continue to play and hope to see the game grow.
